summary: Oracle's private deployment fallback obtained a valid GitHub OIDC identity, but the Live validator admitted only the canonical live-control workflow identity, so the private-deploy workflow failed closed with OIDC_WORKFLOW_REJECTED before KRATOS dispatch. The repair adds exactly the canonical private-deploy workflow identity to the workflow allowlist while preserving repository, owner, ref, runner, event, subject, run, JTI and freshness constraints; the exact fixing head passed Oracle Cloudflare CI and Wrangler deployment validation.
learning_objectives: Bind federated CI authorization to an explicit set of canonical workflow identities instead of one incidental workflow or a broad repository-level trust category.
When extending an identity allowlist, preserve every independent repository, owner, ref, runner, event, subject, replay and freshness constraint rather than widening adjacent authority.
Use positive controls for every intended workflow identity and a negative control proving an otherwise-valid third workflow identity remains rejected.
rejection_reason: Sergeant rejected the PR #165 lesson proposal after the owner-authorized Oracle/workstation council: the Teacher detector copied exact fixing-patch workflow identifiers instead of generalizing, the Defender identified overly broad repository trust as a false-positive risk, and the Defender identified missing explicit negative-control proof for an otherwise-valid third workflow identity.
